slot.brief: Compare rms speeds of two gases at possibly different temperatures; find the ratio using v_rms ∝ √(T/M) with mole data given.

stem: A vessel contains $1\text{ mol}$ of helium gas at $300\text{ K}$, and another vessel contains $4\text{ mol}$ of oxygen gas at $600\text{ K}$. Taking the molar masses of helium and oxygen to be $4\text{ g mol}^{-1}$ and $32\text{ g mol}^{-1}$ respectively, the ratio of the rms speed of helium atoms to that of oxygen molecules is:

verdicts.working: v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M); mole counts irrelevant. Ratio = sqrt((T_He/M_He)/(T_O2/M_O2)) = sqrt((300/4)/(600/32)) = sqrt(75/18.75) = sqrt(4) = 2, i.e. 2:1.

working:
The root-mean-square speed of molecules of an ideal gas is given by:
$$v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$$
Notice that $v_{\text{rms}}$ depends only on the absolute temperature $T$ and the molar mass $M$, and is independent of the number of moles $n$.

Taking the ratio of the rms speed of helium to that of oxygen:
$$\dfrac{v_{\text{rms, He}}}{v_{\text{rms, }\text{O}_2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{T_{\text{He}}}{T_{\text{O}_2}} \times \dfrac{M_{\text{O}_2}}{M_{\text{He}}}}$$

Substitute the given values:
$$\dfrac{v_{\text{rms, He}}}{v_{\text{rms, }\text{O}_2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{300\text{ K}}{600\text{ K}} \times \dfrac{32\text{ g mol}^{-1}}{4\text{ g mol}^{-1}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{2} \times 8} = \sqrt{4} = 2$$

Thus, the ratio is $2 : 1$.

Independent check: v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M); mole counts irrelevant. Ratio = sqrt((T_He/M_He)/(T_O2/M_O2)) = sqrt((300/4)/(600/32)) = sqrt(75/18.75) = sqrt(4) = 2, i.e. 2:1.

draft.distractor_notes:
$1 : 2$ comes from inverting the ratio (calculating oxygen to helium instead of helium to oxygen).
$1 : 1$ comes from incorrectly including the number of moles as $v_{\text{rms}} \propto \sqrt{nT/M}$, yielding $\sqrt{(1 \times 300 \times 32)/(4 \times 600 \times 4)} = 1$.
$4 : 1$ comes from confusing molar mass $M$ with total mass $m = nM$, using $v_{\text{rms}} \propto \sqrt{T/(nM)}$, yielding $\sqrt{(300 \times 4 \times 32)/(600 \times 1 \times 4)} = \sqrt{16} = 4$.
